children.prompt: Show that the perpendicular height $h$ of the pyramid is $12\text{ cm}$.

answer.short:
Let $H$ be the height of $\triangle ABC$.
$$\begin{align*}
H &= \sqrt{12^2 + 9^2} \\
&= \sqrt{225} \\
&= 15
\end{align*}$$
Thus the height of $\triangle ABC$ is $15\text{ cm}$.

content.prompt:
A cone has a radius $20\text{ cm}$ and a total surface area of $3079\text{ cm}^2$.
Find the height $(h)$ of the cone to the nearest whole number.

spec.mathematics: Closed right circular cone. Given radius20cm,totalSA3079cm²; perpendicularheight h unknown. Internalaxis/radius and rightangle retained. No numericalheight/slantgiven added.
spec.drawingCoordinates: Normalized illustrative sourceproportions radius2,height4 are drawingcoordinates only, NOT physicalgivenlengths. Analyticcurvedtemplate derives rimtangentvisibility.

answer.worked:
Let $l$ be the slant height.
$$\begin{align*}
SA &= \pi r^2 + \pi rl \\
3079 &= \pi(20)^2 + \pi(20)l \\
3079 &= 400\pi + 20\pi l \\
l &= \frac{3079 - 400\pi}{20\pi} \\
l &\approx 29.0
\end{align*}$$
Using Pythagoras:
$$\begin{align*}
l^2 &= h^2 + r^2 \\
h &= \sqrt{l^2 - r^2} \\
&= \sqrt{29.0^2 - 20^2} \\
&\approx 21.0
\end{align*}$$
The height is $21\text{ cm}$ to the nearest whole number.

content.prompt:
The roof of this greenhouse is a square pyramid with identical triangular faces.
The sides of the greenhouse are rectangles and there is no floor.
The dimensions of the greenhouse are shown on the diagram.

children.label: i
children.prompt: Sketch a possible net of the greenhouse.

answer.short: A net consisting of 4 rectangles of $12 \times 2$ attached to the base, with a triangle of base 12 and slant height $6.5$ attached to the top of each rectangle, or similar valid arrangement.
answer.worked: A net consisting of 4 rectangles of $12 \times 2$ attached to the base, with a triangle of base 12 and slant height $6.5$ attached to the top of each rectangle, or similar valid arrangement.

children.label: ii
children.prompt: Calculate the surface area of the greenhouse.

answer.short:
$$\begin{align*}
\text{Area of 4 rectangular walls} &= 4 \times (12 \times 2) \\
&= 96 \text{ m}^2 \\
\text{Area of 4 triangular roof faces} &= 4 \times \left(\frac{1}{2} \times 12 \times 6.5\right) \\
&= 156 \text{ m}^2 \\
\text{Total surface area} &= 96 + 156 \\
&= 252 \text{ m}^2
\end{align*}$$
